articles.title: NASSCOM Chief: Green Card Curbs Will Push More Work to India's Talent Base
articles.excerpt: In an exclusive interview, NASSCOM chairperson Srikanth Velamakanni says the US PERM suspension of eight tech firms won't hurt Indian IT's bottom line — and argues that when talent can't move, work will move to where the talent is.
articles.image_caption: A US Permanent Resident Card, commonly known as a green card

sources.label: TradingView News India (Nasscom official statement via newswire)

articles.nri_angle: For the millions of Indian tech professionals on the H-1B-to-green-card track, the NASSCOM chief's message cuts two ways: limited near-term damage to employers, but a signal that the US settlement route is narrowing — making India's own talent economy the fallback plan.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: $400K to Live Comfortably on H-1B? What 10 US Cities Actually Cost in 2026
articles.excerpt: Entrepreneur Aniruddha Anjana's viral breakdown estimates a family of four needs $407,597 a year in San Francisco and $204,672 in Houston to live comfortably in 2026 — personal estimates that expose how fast a six-figure H-1B salary disappears.
articles.image_caption: New York City, one of the 10 US metros analyzed for H-1B living costs
articles.nri_angle: For H-1B workers and families weighing a US move, this reframes the offer letter: the same salary can mean comfort in Houston and strain in San Francisco, so the city matters as much as the number.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Extends $100,000 H-1B Fee to September 2027 as New Order Ties Filings to Employer Layoffs
articles.excerpt: Two September 18 actions reshape the H-1B program: the $100,000 payment policy is extended through September 2027, while a separate executive order directs federal agencies to weigh an employer's layoff history when adjudicating filings.
articles.image_caption: Donald Trump

sources.label: Yale Office of International Students & Scholars

articles.nri_angle: Nearly 70% of H-1B visa holders are Indian; the fee extension and layoff scrutiny directly affect their job mobility and employer's willingness to sponsor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Employers with layoffs face stricter scrutiny.
Labor Department to review past applications.

articles.title: HUD's FHA Crackdown Shuts Out Visa Holders as Home Loans Fall to Near Zero
articles.excerpt: Non-permanent residents went from 5.8% of FHA purchase originations to 0.1% after the May 2025 rule change — and conventional lending has not picked up the slack.
articles.image_caption: The Robert C. Weaver Federal Building, HUD headquarters in Washington, D.C. (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: With Indians receiving roughly 70% of H-1B approvals, the FHA lockout hits the Indian diaspora's largest professional cohort directly — and in exactly the tech markets (San Jose, Salt Lake City, Raleigh) where Indian engineers buy their first American homes.

articles.title: Bodycam Video Shows NYPD Rushing Man Shot by ICE Agent to the Hospital
articles.excerpt: New footage shows officers racing Oscar Belgal, shot in the neck by an ICE agent with his child in the car, to the hospital themselves — as DHS defends the shooting and Mamdani escalates his fight to push ICE out of New York.
articles.image_caption: A still from NYPD body-camera footage released October 9, 2026 shows officers attending to a wounded man on Marble Hill Avenue after an ICE agent shot him. Officers are seen carrying the man to a patrol car to rush him to the hospital.
articles.nri_angle: The case tests how far federal immigration enforcement can go in a sanctuary city, and the bodycam footage is now central evidence in that fight — one immigrant New Yorkers of every background, including the city's large South Asian community, will be watching.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Says US Green Card Curbs 'Do Not Advance' Shared Ambitions
articles.excerpt: The MEA slammed JD Vance's 'indentured servants' remark as deeply offensive and clarified that the PERM suspension will not touch existing H-1B visas — even as green card paths narrow.
articles.image_caption: An MEA official addresses the media during a press briefing in New Delhi. The ministry said on Friday that the latest US green card restrictions did not advance the shared ambitions of India and the United States.
articles.nri_angle: MEA's pushback on US green card curbs directly affects hundreds of thousands of Indians in the US immigration pipeline; the PERM suspension freezes green card routes while leaving H-1B status intact.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICE Agent Shoots Man in NYC; Mamdani Calls Trump, Demands ICE Out
articles.excerpt: An ICE officer shot 28-year-old Oscar Belgal in his car in Marble Hill on Oct. 8 while a 5-year-old child sat inside. Mayor Mamdani spent two hours on the phone with Trump and DHS's Markwayne Mullin trying to free the wounded man — then demanded ICE leave New York City entirely.
articles.image_caption: Zohran Mamdani addresses a rally, alongside scenes from a protest against ICE in New York City. Mamdani called President Trump to demand ICE be pulled out of the city after an ICE agent shot a man in NYC.
articles.nri_angle: The Marble Hill shooting intensifies federal-versus-city immigration enforcement tensions in NYC boroughs where South Asian immigrants live, with Mayor Mamdani framing ICE operations as a public-safety threat to immigrant communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kashmiri Filmmaker Arfat Sheikh Released on Bond After Two Weeks in ICE Detention
articles.excerpt: Sheikh was detained at Washington Dulles airport on September 24; the deportation case against him continues even as his film 'Saffron Kingdom' landed a US distribution deal.
articles.image_caption: Arfat Sheikh speaking at the Teaneck International Film Festival, where he received the Emerging Filmmaker Activist Award in 2025. Sheikh was released from ICE custody on bond on Thursday after two weeks in detention.
articles.nri_angle: Sheikh's case spotlights how the US immigration crackdown is ensnaring long-resident Indian-origin artists with pending asylum cases and work authorization.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Says US Green Card Suspension Won't Disrupt Workforce Strategy or Hiring
articles.excerpt: TCS says its PERM filings were in the single digits over the past two years, while Washington freezes green card labor certifications for eight major IT employers, including Infosys, Wipro, HCL, and Cognizant.
articles.image_caption: TCS's statement to Indian stock exchanges dated October 9, 2026, alongside the company logo. The company said its PERM applications were in single digits over the last two years and that it plans to hire 15,000 people in the US over the next five years.
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian H-1B holders at the eight suspended firms lose their employer-sponsored green card route, leaving them stuck on temporary status in decade-long backlogs.

articles.title: Microsoft Disputes Vance's 'Foreign Indentured Servants' Claim With Its Own H-1B Data
articles.excerpt: In a Thursday-afternoon statement, the company said 80% of its H-1B filings last year were extensions for existing employees, not new hires; Vance says the fraud task force has opened multiple criminal investigations.
articles.image_caption: US Vice President JD Vance, whose claim that H-1B workers are 'foreign indentured servants' Microsoft disputed with its own H-1B hiring data.
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian H-1B professionals at the eight named firms face frozen PERM applications, the critical bridge to green cards; Microsoft's rebuttal and the criminal investigations will decide whether the freeze holds.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada Puts $20 Million Behind Fast Track to Ontario Licences for Foreign-Trained Doctors
articles.excerpt: Health Canada's October 7 funding expands Practice Ready Ontario, letting experienced internationally trained physicians qualify for family medicine through a 12-week clinical assessment instead of a two-year residency.
articles.image_caption: A physician consults with a patient in a medical clinic in Ontario. Health Canada committed $20 million on October 7, 2026, to expand the Practice Ready Ontario fast track for internationally trained doctors.
articles.nri_angle: India-trained doctors are among the largest groups of internationally trained physicians in Canada; the 12-week fast track to Ontario licensing directly addresses the licensing barriers that have kept thousands out of medicine.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Suspends Microsoft, Adobe and Six IT Firms From Green Card Program
articles.excerpt: Vice President JD Vance announced the PERM suspension at the White House, accusing the firms of replacing laid-off Americans with foreign workers; thousands of Indians in green-card backlogs face fresh uncertainty.
articles.image_caption: Signage of Wipro, Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys and HCL — four of the firms suspended from the US green-card programme. The White House said no new or pending PERM applications involving the named companies will be processed.
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian professionals at Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini can no longer advance their green-card status through their employer — a direct hit on the largest block of Indians in U.S. immigration backlogs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: October Visa Bulletin Restores EB-2 India, but Green Card Wait Still Tops 11 Years
articles.excerpt: The State Department’s October 2026 Visa Bulletin reopens EB-2 India and moves EB-1 forward as fiscal 2027 numbers arrive — but Indian applicants still face cutoffs more than a decade behind the rest of the world.
articles.image_caption: A U.S. permanent resident card (green card). The October 2026 Visa Bulletin restores EB-2 India and advances EB-1, though Indian applicants still face final-action cutoffs more than 11 years behind most other countries.
articles.nri_angle: The October bulletin gives Indian professionals stuck on H-1B status for years a rare concrete opening — a filing window that can unlock work authorization, travel flexibility, and job-change portability even as the underlying decade-long backlog persists.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DHS Formally Publishes $70,000-per-Student OPT Fee Proposal, Schools on Hook
articles.excerpt: The rule moves from White House review to formal publication: universities — not students — would pay $70,000 per initial OPT application and $30,000 per renewal, totaling about $100,000 over three years. A 60-day comment period opens now, with lawsuits expected.
articles.image_caption: Graduates in caps are silhouetted during a graduation ceremony. International graduates seeking post-study work authorization would be subject to the proposed $70,000-per-student OPT fee paid by their universities.
articles.nri_angle: Indian students are the largest national cohort of international students in the US, and OPT is the primary bridge from American degrees to H-1B careers for Indian graduates — a $70,000-per-student fee charged to universities directly threatens that study-work pathway.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Award-Winning Kashmiri Filmmaker Arfat Sheikh Detained by ICE at Dulles Airport
articles.excerpt: The 42-year-old director of "Saffron Kingdom" was arrested September 24 after arriving from California; DHS says he overstayed lawful admittance, while his supporters say he had a pending immigration application and work authorization.
articles.image_caption: The main terminal of Washington Dulles International Airport at dusk. Kashmiri filmmaker Arfat Sheikh was detained by ICE at Dulles on arrival.
articles.nri_angle: The ICE detention of an award-winning Kashmiri filmmaker with a pending asylum application signals heightened risk for immigrants in legal limbo; DHS says a pending application does not confer legal status.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: JD Vance Calls H-1B Visa Programme 'Completely Broken,' Backs Scrapping It
articles.excerpt: The vice president said he would support eliminating the H-1B system, days after a second federal judge blocked the administration's $100,000 visa fee and an executive order tightened scrutiny of sponsoring firms.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Vice President JD Vance, right, speaks during an interview aboard Air Force Two, with the vice-presidential seal visible on the cabin wall. In the interview, Vance said he would support eliminating the H-1B visa programme, calling it “completely broken.”
articles.nri_angle: Indians are the largest group of H-1B beneficiaries; talk of eliminating the programme creates direct uncertainty for Indian professionals' renewals, job mobility and green-card prospects.

articles.title: Indian Workers Begin Signing Payout Deals in €31 Million Milan Consulate Settlement
articles.excerpt: Nearly 300 workers, most recruited in India, will receive an average of €50,000 each in back pay and damages after prosecutors found they were paid less than $2 an hour on the U.S. consulate construction site.
articles.image_caption: Scaffolding covers the construction site of the new U.S. Consulate General in Milan, with a worker in an orange vest visible on the structure. Prosecutors found that nearly 300 workers on the project, most recruited in India, were paid less than $2 an hour, and workers have begun signing payout deals under a nearly €31 million settlement.
articles.nri_angle: Most of the exploited workers were recruited in India; the settlement shows how overseas Indian labourers can use host-country legal protections to recover wages and secure residence status.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ontario Calls in Police as College Recruitment Pipeline Under Scrutiny
articles.excerpt: Ontario has referred suspected criminal misuse of student financial aid at private career colleges to provincial police, after inspectors linked student accounts and $219 million in public funds to a network of immigration recruitment firms.
articles.image_caption: An Ontario Provincial Police cruiser. Ontario has referred suspected criminal misuse of student financial aid at private career colleges to the OPP for investigation.
articles.nri_angle: Indian students are the primary market for the recruitment pipeline under scrutiny; families paying lakhs in agent fees face the greatest losses when colleges lose aid eligibility or collapse.

articles.image_caption: Image: @USCIS via X
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals form the largest employment-based green card cohort with years-long backlogs, making them the likeliest casualties of policies that penalize staying in the US while an application is pending.

articles.title: Reported $100,000 OPT Fee Nears Publication, Putting International Students' Work Rights at Risk
articles.excerpt: The Department of Homeland Security's proposed "Optional Practical Training Fees" rule has cleared White House review and could soon be published for public comment — attaching a reported six-figure price tag to the post-graduation work program used by hundreds of thousands of foreign graduates each year.
articles.image_caption: A graphic illustrating the proposed $100,000 fee on the Optional Practical Training program for international graduates. The DHS proposal cleared White House review on September 11, 2026 and now awaits publication in the Federal Register.
articles.nri_angle: With 363,019 Indian students in the US — the largest international student cohort — a six-figure OPT fee would fall hardest on Indian families financing American degrees and the STEM pipeline they feed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Asylum Win Caps Immigrant's Two-Year Detention as Courts Weigh Third-Country Deportations
articles.excerpt: Celestin Dima fled torture in Burkina Faso, won protection from deportation — and was then held for two years while ICE shopped for a third country to take him. His asylum grant comes as the Supreme Court lets the practice resume.
articles.image_caption: The Karnes County Residential Center in Texas, an ICE detention facility. Burkina Faso asylum-seeker Celestin Dima spent more than two years in ICE detention before winning his case.
articles.nri_angle: The case is a window into the detention-and-deportation machinery that also ensnares South Asian asylum-seekers; the Supreme Court's December arguments on third-country removals and mandatory detention will shape the landscape for every immigrant community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GOP Congressman Calls His Own Atlanta District an H-1B Fraud 'Hotspot,' Seeks Federal Probe
articles.excerpt: Rep. Rich McCormick's letter to the Trump administration lands amid the most aggressive H-1B enforcement campaign in the program's history, with a nationwide fraud probe and a 48% surge in investigations.
articles.image_caption: Rep. Rich McCormick (R-Ga.), who called his own Atlanta district a suspected H-1B fraud 'hotspot' and is seeking a federal probe.
articles.nri_angle: Indians are the largest group of H-1B holders; the Atlanta fraud probe adds to an enforcement wave — site visits, workforce audits, reluctant sponsors — that directly affects Indian tech workers' job security and documentation burden.

articles.title: US Moves to Strip Citizenship From 40 People in Largest Denaturalization Push Yet
articles.excerpt: The Justice Department filed 40 denaturalization cases between Aug. 21 and Oct. 2 against naturalized citizens accused of serious crimes and immigration fraud — the biggest such push in modern US history.
articles.image_caption: A U.S. passport. The government has moved to strip citizenship from 40 people in the largest denaturalization drive in decades.
articles.nri_angle: One Indian national is named among the 40 denaturalization targets, and the sweeping push puts the large Indian naturalized population and N-400 applicants on notice that concealment on immigration forms — however old — can now trigger loss of citizenship.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Radiology Groups Join Coalition Against $103,265 H-1B Fee on Physicians
articles.excerpt: The American College of Radiology and dozens of physician and patient advocacy groups told federal immigration officials the proposed fee would make it harder to recruit doctors for rural and underserved communities.
articles.image_caption: An MRI scanner in a hospital radiology suite. Radiology groups are urging the Trump administration to exempt physicians from the new $100,000 H-1B fee.
articles.nri_angle: The fee would hit hardest at safety-net hospitals and rural practices that rely on international medical graduates, a workforce that includes many Indian-trained physicians working in the US on H-1B status.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: September's Global Immigration Shifts: What Changed for Visa Seekers Worldwide
articles.excerpt: From Australia's new skilled-visa priority rules to Japan's twentyfold permanent residence fee hike and a UK settlement overhaul on the horizon, September brought rule changes that directly affect Indian migrants.
articles.image_caption: WR Immigration's September 2026 global immigration recap graphic. The recap covers rule changes in Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Japan, Saudi Arabia, New Zealand, and Thailand.
articles.nri_angle: Australia's onshore-first processing favors Indian students and graduates already in the country, while the UK's coming earned-settlement overhaul could reshape ILR eligibility for thousands of Indians nearing five years of residence.

articles.title: Montana Governor Lands in India to Rescue Lentil Exports Amid MAGA Backlash
articles.excerpt: Governor Greg Gianforte is leading a 30-member delegation to India and Sri Lanka to rebuild the state's collapsed pulse trade, even as anti-India voices in his own party attack the trip.
articles.image_caption: Montana Governor Greg Gianforte. He is leading a 30-plus member delegation to India and Sri Lanka, with reviving Montana's lentil exports to India the centerpiece of the trip.
articles.nri_angle: The trip exposes a paradox for Indian Americans: anti-India voices demand the governor's impeachment while Montana's farm economy and universities actively court Indian consumers, students, and research ties.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Extends $100K H-1B Fee to 2027 Even as Courts Block Collection
articles.excerpt: The Sept. 18 extension keeps the $100,000 H-1B payment alive through Sept. 2027 — but two federal judges have barred agencies from collecting it while the administration's appeal plays out.
articles.image_caption: A close-up of a U.S. visa foil showing the H-1B visa type. The Trump administration extended the $100,000 payment on new overseas H-1B petitions through Sept. 2027, though federal courts have barred its collection.
articles.nri_angle: Indians receive roughly three-quarters of H-1B visas, so the $100,000 fee on new overseas hires would land hardest on Indian tech workers — for now the courts have kept it off the books, but the legal limbo is delaying adjudications.

articles.title: Trump H-1B Fee Fight Heads to a Showdown Over Congress's Authority
articles.excerpt: Judges in Massachusetts and California have ruled the $100,000 fee amounts to a tax only Congress can impose; the administration has responded with a new $103,265 rulemaking that 22 states oppose.

articles.title: Mother of US Green Card Holder Denied Visitor Visa: 214(b) Rules and Interview Tips
articles.excerpt: A Green Card holder's mother was refused a B1/B2 visitor visa within minutes at the Mumbai consulate despite showing savings, property and investments. Reddit users - and the 214(b) rule itself - say it was never about money at all.
articles.image_caption: The US Embassy in New Delhi. The mother of a US green card holder was denied a visitor visa under Section 214(b).
articles.nri_angle: Green Card holders and US citizens inviting parents over must build the case around the parent's roots in India - steady income, property, a short specific itinerary - because a 214(b) denial has no appeal, only a stronger reapplication.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Decade-Long Study Finds H-1B Workers Paid 15% Less Than Peers
articles.excerpt: Harvard economist George Borjas's analysis of 2014–2024 records finds visa holders better educated but underpaid — though critics say the wage gap is far smaller than claimed.
articles.image_caption: H-1B visa workers, who a decade-long study found are paid 15% less than their peers
articles.nri_angle: The wage-gap debate bears directly on Indian professionals, the largest group of H-1B beneficiaries, as the fate of the $100,000 fee will shape U.S. employer sponsorship in coming years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DACA and TPS Holders Face Tougher Travel Rules After Immigration Appeals Board Ruling
articles.excerpt: The August decision overturns a 12-year-old rule — advance parole trips can now trigger three- or 10-year bars on reentry to the United States.
articles.image_caption: Supporters at a DACA rally. A Board of Immigration Appeals ruling means DACA and TPS holders who leave the US could trigger reentry bars.
articles.nri_angle: Indian DACA recipients and adjustment-of-status applicants lose a once-safe travel option, raising the stakes of every family visit home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russia to Take 70,000 Indian Skilled Workers This Year, Jaishankar Tells Parliament Panel
articles.excerpt: The external affairs minister's briefing covered trade, energy and Ukraine diplomacy — plus India's push to bring home citizens recruited into Russia's military.
articles.image_caption: S. Jaishankar, India's External Affairs Minister, who told Parliament that Russia will take 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year.
articles.nri_angle: The 70,000-worker commitment opens a major new overseas employment channel for Indians, alongside the government's effort to repatriate those fraudulently recruited into Russia's military.
